boundedSliceCharter.behavior: Add ONE new Playwright spec (recommended: e2e/saved-custom-combat-launch.spec.ts, sibling to and reusing the setup pattern of e2e/saved-custom-combat.spec.ts) that: (1) creates a server-saved custom unit via POST /api/units/custom exactly as saved-custom-combat.spec.ts does; (2) creates a campaign through the real wizard with that saved design in the roster; (3) navigates to /gameplay/campaigns/:id/missions/:missionId/launch and asserts mission-readiness-panel shows the custom unit ready; (4) CLICKS launch-mission-direct (the step every existing spec stops short of); (5) follows the resulting /gameplay/encounters/:id route through launch-encounter-btn -> pre-battle -> auto-resolve-btn (cheapest terminal path, mirroring encounter-combat-continuity.spec.ts's first test) -> asserts game-completed; (6) navigates to the review screen, asserts post-battle-review-screen, clicks apply-outcome-cta; (7) reads back GET /api/campaigns/:id and asserts the roster still carries the same rosterId/unitRef/unitSource:'custom' triple, and that a page reload preserves it -- i.e. reproduces exactly the roadmap's acceptance line 1 ('actual server-saved biped custom launch, commands, terminal flow and durable post-battle state alongside canonical comparison'). A second, minimal case (or a parametrized second run within the same spec) repeats the identical route with a CANONICAL unit id only, to give the 'alongside canonical comparison' clause its own explicit witness rather than relying on encounter-combat-continuity.spec.ts's different fixture path as an implicit comparison.

boundedSliceCharter.whatTurnsRed: This is new coverage, not a regression re-run, so 'red-first' here means: write the test against current origin/main BEFORE any product change, run it, and let its natural failure point (if any) reveal whether EncounterService's custom-unit seeding actually reaches this specific browser route end-to-end. Per productionRouteAndCodeCitations above, the expectation (not yet proven by an actual run) is that it passes with ZERO product changes, because every hop in the route already has real, tested, unconditional production code. If it fails, the failure's exact hop (readiness panel never shows ready, launch-mission-direct stays disabled, the encounter never launches, or the roster loses unitSource='custom' after apply-outcome) IS the reproduction and names the file to fix.

buildRunInvocationCorrection.verifiedFindingThisSession: grep -rn 3639 across the entire repository (excluding node_modules) returned ZERO matches -- no file, script, or config in this repo references port 3639. The repo's actual e2e webServer convention, read directly from scripts/playwright/run-playwright.mjs:34-51, is: the DEV e2e server runs on the default PORT the dev server binds (not overridden by run-playwright.mjs itself), and the OPTIONAL --prod-evidence flag (which run-playwright.mjs explicitly strips before forwarding to the Playwright CLI) builds and starts `.next/standalone/server.js` on PORT 3600 via `npx kill-port 3600 --silent && npm run build && node .next/standalone/server.js`. This is flagged as UNVERIFIED-AGAINST-SOURCE per this project's own verify-never-infer rule rather than silently corrected without comment: the orchestrating instruction's '3639' and 'standalone server' pairing does not match anything in this repository as of be7f85b86. The recommended invocation above (node scripts/playwright/run-playwright.mjs test --project=chromium e2e/saved-custom-combat-launch.spec.ts --workers=1, WITHOUT --prod-evidence) matches the exact convention every sibling combat/campaign spec in package.json (qc:campaign-long:browser, qc:command:browser:quick, verify:qc:encounter-combat-continuity, etc.) already uses -- default dev-mode webServer, not the standalone/production server, and never --prod-evidence.
